record.title: Bounded excess-height conjecture for 3-sphere triangulations
record.statement: Let $\mathscr{P}_1(S^3)$ be the graph whose nodes are one-vertex triangulations of the 3-sphere, arranged by level $n$, and let a simplification path be a path reducing the level to a minimal triangulation. The **excess height** of such a path is the maximum level reached above its starting level. **Bounded excess-height conjecture.** From any node at any level $n \geq 3$ of the graph $\mathscr{P}_1(S^3)$, there is a simplification path of excess height $\leq 2$. If true, this would help explain the practical ease of simplifying 3-sphere triangulations and would improve known bounds on the number of Pachner moves needed for simplification. The conjecture is supported by the absence of known pathological 3-sphere triangulations requiring more than two extra tetrahedra, but remains open.
record.source_name: Benjamin A. Burton, “Simplification paths in the Pachner graphs of closed orientable 3-manifold triangulations”, arXiv:1110.6080 (2011).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2011). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1011.4169](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.4169).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.6080

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

record.title: Huang–Sudakov's biclique partition–chromatic number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **biclique partition number** is the minimum number of bicliques, that is, complete bipartite graphs, needed to partition the edge set of $G$. Its chromatic number $chi(G)$ is the minimum number of stable sets in a partition of the vertex set of $G$.

**Huang–Sudakov's conjecture.** For each integer $k>0$, there exists a graph $G$ with biclique partition number $k$ and chromatic number at least

$$
2^{c \log^2 k},
$$

for some constant $c>0$.

If true, this graph-theoretical statement would improve the known lower bound on the nondeterministic communication complexity of the clique-versus-stable-set problem from $\frac{6}{5}\log n-O(1)$ to $\Omega(\log^2 n)$. The exact deterministic and nondeterministic communication complexities remain unknown.
record.source_name: Samuel Fiorini, Volker Kaibel, Kanstantsin Pashkovich and Dirk Oliver Theis, “Combinatorial Bounds on Nonnegative Rank and Extended Formulations”, arXiv:1111.0444 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.0444

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).

record.title: González–Zarati lower-bound conjecture for biequivariant maps
record.statement:
Let $\alpha(m)$ denote the number of ones in the binary expansion of $m$, and let $b(n,e)$ be the smallest positive integer $r$ for which there is a $\mathbb{Z}_{2^e}$-biequivariant map $S^{2n+1}\times S^{2n+1}\to S^{2r+1}$. **González–Zarati conjecture.** For $1\leq e\leq\alpha(m)$,

$$
b(m+\alpha(m)-e,e)\geq 2m-\alpha(m)+e-1.
$$

This conjecture gives lower bounds for biequivariant maps and, through the relationship with immersion dimensions and the topological complexity of lens spaces, would imply corresponding lower bounds for those invariants. The source presents it as a conjecture from González and Zarati; its resolution is not specified here.
record.source_name: Jesus Gonzalez, Maurilio Velasco and W. Stephen Wilson, “Biequivariant Maps on Spheres and Topological Complexity of Lens Spaces”, arXiv:1111.4669 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4669

record.title: Four-bend necessity conjecture for planar graph EPG representations
record.statement: An **EPG representation** of a graph represents each vertex by a path in the square grid, with adjacency corresponding to sharing a grid edge; a path has a bend at each change of grid direction. **Four-bend necessity conjecture.** There exists a planar graph $G$ such that every EPG representation of $G$ contains at least one path with four bends. The source places this statement in the conclusions alongside the open determination of the maximum bend-number of planar graphs, while its preceding theorem establishes only that this maximum is either three or four.
record.source_name: Daniel Heldt, Kolja Knauer and Torsten Ueckerdt, “On the bend-number of planar and outerplanar graphs”, arXiv:1112.3353 (2011).

record.title: Bondy's conjecture on long circuits generating the cycle space
record.statement:
Let $d\in\mathbb{Z}$, let $X$ be a vertex-3-connected graph with $f_0(X)$ vertices, and let $\delta(X)$ be its minimum degree. Write $\mathrm{Z}_1(X;\mathbb{Z}/2)$ for the cycle space of $X$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$.

**Bondy's conjecture.** If

$$
f_0(X)\geq 2d\qquad\text{and}\qquad \delta(X)\geq d,
$$

then the set of all circuits of length at least $2d-1$ is a $\mathbb{Z}/2$-generating system of $\mathrm{Z}_1(X;\mathbb{Z}/2)$.

The conjecture proposes that sufficiently long circuits generate the entire cycle space of a sufficiently dense, vertex-3-connected graph. The source notes that Locke proved it under the additional assumption that $X$ is non-Hamiltonian or $f_0(X)\geq 4d-5$; the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Peter C. Heinig, “On prisms, Möbius ladders and the cycle space of dense graphs”, arXiv:1112.5101 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.5101

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2011).

record.title: The impossibility of exactly simplifying the floor quotient below the square root
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number and let $a$ be an integer satisfying $1<a<p$. Consider the quotient $\left\lfloor \frac{p}{a}\right\rfloor$ for $a\leq\left\lfloor\sqrt{p}\right\rfloor$. **Impossibility conjecture.** It is impossible to find any exact simplification for

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{p}{a}\right\rfloor
$$

when $a\leq\left\lfloor\sqrt{p}\right\rfloor$. The claim concerns the distribution of first-order focals in the geometric view of the sieve of Eratosthenes; no resolution or supporting result is supplied in the excerpt.
record.source_name: Alexandru Iosif, “A Geometric View of the Sieve of Eratosthenes”, arXiv:1112.5796 (2026).

record.title: Convex hull conjecture for non-wandering sets of open billiards
record.statement:
For $i\ne j$, let $(p_{ij},p_{ji})\in K_i\times K_j$ be a pair realizing the minimum distance between $K_i$ and $K_j$. Let

$$
H=\operatorname{Cvx}\{p_{ij}:1\le i,j\le u,\,i\ne j\}
$$

be their convex hull. Let $1\le \alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\le u$ with $n\ge 3$, and let $(q_1,\ldots,q_n)$ be a periodic billiard trajectory such that $q_j\in K_{\alpha_k}$ for each $j$. **Convex hull conjecture.** Each $q_j$ is contained in $H$. Furthermore, the non-wandering set $M_0$ is contained in $H$. This proposed containment would restrict the non-wandering set to a smaller region and could relax the conditions needed for the dimension estimates; the source does not establish the conjecture.
record.source_name: Paul Wright, “Estimates of Hausdorff dimension for non-wandering sets of higher dimensional open billiards”, arXiv:1112.6066 (2011).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.6066

record.title: Perverse-filtration and Cherednik-filtration conjecture for compactified Jacobians
record.statement:
For coprime positive integers $k,n$, let $L_{k/n}$ be the finite-dimensional simple representation of the rational Cherednik algebra with parameter $k/n$, let $eL_{k/n}$ be its spherical part, and let $\Lambda^{i,j}$ denote the filtration of Proposition CEE. Let the cohomology of the compactified Jacobian of the singularity $X^n=Y^k$ carry its perverse filtration. **Perverse-filtration conjecture.** The perverse filtration and the filtration $\Lambda$ of Proposition CEE agree.

This identification would connect the geometric perverse filtration with the representation-theoretic filtration used to compute torus-knot homology. The source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Alexei Oblomkov, Jacob Rasmussen and Vivek Shende, “The Hilbert scheme of a plane curve singularity and the HOMFLY homology of its link”, arXiv:1201.2115 (2012).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2115

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2012). “The bivariate polynomial $$C_{n}^{(m)}(q,t):=\spp_{\mbox {\rm \tiny DAHA}}(T(n,mn+1),a=0)$$ was introduced by A. Garsia and M.”

record.title: The square-root agreement-subtree conjecture for balanced phylogenetic trees
record.statement:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be balanced, rooted, binary trees of height $m$. An **agreement subtree** is a common subtree of the two trees on a shared set of leaves. **The square-root agreement-subtree conjecture.** Any two balanced, rooted, binary trees of height $m$ have an agreement subtree on at least

$$
2^{m/2}
$$

leaves. This would establish the conjectured square-root exponent for the maximum agreement subtree problem in the rooted balanced case; the statement is presented as a belief in the source and no resolution is given there.
record.source_name: Daniel M. Martin and Bhalchandra D. Thatte, “The maximum agreement subtree problem”, arXiv:1201.5168 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.5168

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

record.title: The rank bound conjecture for tree-automatic well-founded partial orders
record.statement:
A **well-founded partial order** is a partial order with no infinite descending sequence. Its **rank** is the ordinal rank obtained by assigning to each element the supremum of the ranks of its predecessors plus one, and taking the supremum over all elements. A partial order is **tree-automatic** when its domain and order relation are recognized by finite tree automata.

**Rank bound conjecture.** Every tree-automatic well-founded partial order has rank below

$$
\omega^{\omega^\omega}.
$$

The paper proves this bound for tree-automatic well-founded wulpos and forests, and shows that it is optimal for tree-automatic well-founded trees and wulpos. The conjecture remains open for arbitrary tree-automatic well-founded partial orders; later examples show that forbidding infinite linear suborders does not suffice to obtain the stronger bound $\omega^\omega$.
record.source_name: Martin Huschenbett, Alexander Kartzow, Jiamou Liu and Markus Lohrey, “Tree-Automatic Well-Founded Trees”, arXiv:1201.5495 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.5495

record.title: The miracle of Atiyah bundles
record.statement:
Let $E/\mathbb F_q$ be an elliptic curve, and let $I_r$ denote the indecomposable degree-zero Atiyah bundle of rank $r$. For a decomposition into multiplicities $\bigoplus_{j=1}^s I_{r_j}^{\oplus m_j}$, write $h^0(E,-)$ for its space of global sections and $\operatorname{Aut}(-)$ for its automorphism group. **Miracle of $I_r$.** For every nonnegative integer $n$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\sum_{i=1}^s r_i m_i=n+1}&\frac{q^{h^0(E,\bigoplus_{j=1}^sI_{r_j}^{\oplus m_j})}-1}{\#\operatorname{Aut}(\bigoplus_{j=1}^sI_{r_j}^{\oplus m_j})} =\sum_{\sum_{i=1}^s r_i m_i=n}\frac{1}{\#\operatorname{Aut}(\bigoplus_{j=1}^sI_{r_j}^{\oplus m_j})} \\
&=\frac{q^{\frac{n(n+1)}{2}}}{(q^{n+1}-1)(q^n-1)(q^{n-1}-1)\cdots(q-1)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The identity is motivated by the preceding calculation of automorphism groups and Hom-spaces using Atiyah’s multiplicative structure. The supplied text does not indicate whether it is conjectural or proved.
record.source_name: Lin Weng, “Zeta Functions for Elliptic Curves I. Counting Bundles”, arXiv:1202.0870 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.0870

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).

record.title: Bridge-index conjecture for discrete Morse vectors of knots
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot with bridge index $b$. Say that a $d$-complex has discrete Morse vector $(c_0,\ldots,c_d)$ if it admits a discrete Morse function with exactly $c_i$ critical faces of dimension $i$. **Bridge-index conjecture.** The knot $K$ appears in both of the following ways:

1. As a knotted spanning edge in some $3$-ball with discrete Morse vector $(1,b-2,b-2,0)$, if $b\geq 2$.
2. As a $3$-edge subcomplex of some $3$-sphere with discrete Morse vector $(1,b-3,b-3,1)$, if $b\geq 3$.

The claim is presented as a conjectural consequence suggested by the knot-theoretical approach, relating bridge index to the minimum number of critical faces in a discrete Morse function. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Karim Adiprasito and Bruno Benedetti, “Tight complexes in 3-space admit perfect discrete Morse functions”, arXiv:1202.3390 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.3390

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2012). “This is in fact an open problem, already for $d = 4$.”

record.title: Periodicity conjecture for weighted finite taking-no-breaking games
record.statement:
Let $O=(n_1n_2\dots n_t,p_1p_2\dots p_t)$ and $P=(m_1m_2\dots m_l,q_1q_2\dots q_l)$ be two finite taking-no-breaking octal games. Assume that at least one $n_s$ is neither $0$ nor $1$, and that whenever $n_i$ and $m_j$ are in $\{1,2,3\}$, the corresponding scores satisfy $p_i=i$ and $q_j=j$, while otherwise $p_i=q_j=0$. Let $k$ be the largest entry in $O$ such that $n_k\neq 0,1$. **Taking-no-breaking periodicity conjecture.** Then

$$
\mathcal{G}_s(n+2k+_{\ell}m)=\mathcal{G}_s(n+_{\ell}m).
$$

Here $+_{\ell}$ denotes disjunctive sum, and the conjecture asserts that the period is $2k$ even after adding the fixed game $m$. The authors report strong computational evidence but say that proving the claim is surprisingly difficult; the conjecture is open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Fraser Stewart, “Impartial Scoring Play Games”, arXiv:1202.4655 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).

record.title: Tight cover-time conjecture for minimum-degree weighting
record.statement:
Let $G_w$ be a graph equipped with the minimum-degree weighting scheme, let $n$ be its number of vertices, and let $d$ be the parameter used in the locally tree-like analysis. Let $\text{{\bf COV}}[G_w]$ denote the resulting weighted random walk's cover time. **Tight minimum-degree weighted cover-time conjecture.** The bound in the source can be replaced by

$$
\text{{\bf COV}}[G_w] \leq (1+o(1))\frac{d-1}{d-2}\;n\log n.
$$

This is presented as a sharper bound than the preceding weighted cover-time estimate. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Mohammed Abdullah, “The Cover Time of Random Walks on Graphs”, arXiv:1202.5569 (2012).

record.title: Sudderth–Wainwright–Willsky conjecture on the Bethe partition function
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,\mathcal{A})$ be a factor graph and let $f:\mathbb{\{0,1\}}^n\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ admit a pairwise, log-supermodular factorization over $G$. Let $Z(G)=\sum_x f(x)$ be the true partition function, and let $Z_\mathrm{B}(G)$ denote the maximum Bethe approximation over the local marginal polytope.

**Sudderth–Wainwright–Willsky conjecture.** If $f$ admits a pairwise, log-supermodular factorization over $G$, then

$$
Z_\mathrm{B}(G)\leq Z(G).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the Bethe partition function is a lower bound on the true partition function for attractive pairwise binary graphical models. The paper studies this conjecture and proves the bound under the stated log-supermodularity assumptions.
record.source_name: Nicholas Ruozzi, “The Bethe Partition Function of Log-supermodular Graphical Models”, arXiv:1202.6035 (2012).
record.references:

record.title: Minimal-start conjecture for geometric-arithmetic progressions
record.statement:
A geometric-arithmetic progression (GAP-$k$) is a sequence of $k$ primes of the form

$$
\left\{p_1 r^j+j d\right\}_{j=0}^{k-1},
$$

where $p_1$ is the starting prime, $r$ is the ratio, and $d$ is the difference. A GAP-$k$ is **minimal** when its starting prime and ratio are both the smallest prime $p$ satisfying $p\geq k$.

**Minimal-start conjecture.** The minimal starting prime $p_1$ in a GAP-$k$ is the smallest prime satisfying $p_1\geq k$.

This conjecture concerns the smallest possible starting prime for geometric-arithmetic progressions of a given order. The source provides numerical data and structural motivation but no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Sameen Ahmed Khan, “Primes in Geometric-Arithmetic Progression”, arXiv:1203.2083 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2012).

record.title: Minimal-start-and-ratio conjecture for geometric-arithmetic progressions
record.statement:
A geometric-arithmetic progression (GAP-$k$) is a sequence of $k$ primes of the form

$$
\left\{p_1 r^j+j d\right\}_{j=0}^{k-1},
$$

where $p_1$ is the starting prime, $r$ is the ratio, and $d$ is the difference. A GAP-$k$ is **minimal** when its starting prime and ratio are equal to the smallest prime $p$ satisfying $p\geq k$.

**Minimal-start-and-ratio conjecture.** The minimal starting prime $p_1$ and minimal ratio $r$ in a GAP-$k$ are the smallest prime satisfying $p\geq k$, with $p_1=r$.

The conjecture extends the claim about the starting prime to the ratio and is motivated by examples of minimal GAPs and computational data in the source. No proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Sameen Ahmed Khan, “Primes in Geometric-Arithmetic Progression”, arXiv:1203.2083 (2012).

record.title: The normal-order conjecture for iterated Carmichael lambda values
record.statement:
Let $\lambda(n)$ be the Carmichael lambda function, defined as the exponent of $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^{\times}$, and define its iterates by

$$
\lambda_0(n)=n,\qquad \lambda_k(n)=\lambda(\lambda_{k-1}(n))\quad (k\geq 1).
$$

Let $L(n)$ be the smallest non-negative integer $k$ such that $\lambda_k(n)=1$. The **normal-order conjecture for $L(n)$.** The normal order of $L(n)$ is $e\log\log n$.
This is motivated by a probabilistic model for the related Pratt-tree height $H(p)$, whose conjectured normal order is $e\log\log p$. The paper provides evidence for the corresponding assertion for $L(n)$, while the stated normal-order claim remains open.
record.source_name: Nick Harland, “The number of iterates of the Carmichael lambda function required to reach 1”, arXiv:1203.4791 (2012).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.4791

record.title: The conjecture on the sharp norm of the Bergman projection
record.statement:
Let $n>1$ and $\beta$ be the (semi) norm for which the Bergman projection $P_\alpha$ has norm $\|P_\alpha\|_{\tilde\beta}=\tilde C_{\alpha,n}$. With $C_{\alpha,n}$ as in Theorem Mait, one has the estimate

$$
\frac{\pi}{2}C_{\alpha,n}\leq \tilde C_{\alpha,n}\leq \frac{\sqrt{\pi^2+4}}{2}C_{\alpha,n}.
$$

**Sharp Bergman projection norm conjecture.** The upper quantity is expected to attain the lower bound:

$$
\tilde C_{\alpha,n}=\frac{\pi}{2}C_{\alpha,n}.
$$

This would determine the exact $\tilde\beta$-norm of the Bergman projection and sharpen the estimates in Theorem Mait. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: David Kalaj and Marijan Markovic, “Norm of the Bergman projection”, arXiv:1203.6009 (2012).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.6009

record.title: The toroidal no-three-in-line conjecture involving the divisor function
record.statement: Let $a(n)$ be the smallest multiple of the number of divisors of $n$ that is greater than or equal to $n$. On an $n\times n$ discrete torus, points are required to have no three in a line, meaning that no three points lie in a coset of a cyclic subgroup of the torus. **Toroidal no-three-in-line conjecture.** Given an $n\times n$ discrete torus, one can place $a(n)$ points with no three being in a line. This conjecture proposes a general lower bound for the maximum size of a no-three-in-line configuration on a discrete torus; the paper computes several small cases but does not establish the assertion in general.
record.source_name: Jim Fowler, Andrew Groot, Deven Pandya and Bart Snapp, “The no-three-in-line problem on a torus”, arXiv:1203.6604 (2012).

record.title: The largest-entry-free determinant bound for positive diagonally balanced symmetric matrices
record.statement:
Let $J$ be a positive, diagonally balanced symmetric matrix, and let $S$ denote the comparison matrix used in the determinant bound. **Largest-entry-free determinant conjecture.** One has

$$
\frac{\det(J)}{\prod_{i=1}^n J_{ii}}\leq\frac{\det(S)}{(n-1)^n}=2\left(1-\frac{1}{n-1}\right)^{n-1}\to\frac{2}{e}.
$$

This conjecture is stated as removing dependence on the largest entry from part (b) of the paper's determinant bound; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Christopher J. Hillar, Shaowei Lin and Andre Wibisono, “Inverses of symmetric, diagonally dominant positive matrices and applications”, arXiv:1203.6812 (2013).

record.title: UGA VIGRE conjecture on the complexity of Specht modules
record.statement: Let $S^\lambda$ be a Specht module in a block $B$ of weight $w$. Say that a partition is **$p\times p$** if both it and its conjugate are of the form $p\tau$, equivalently, if its Young diagram is a union of $p\times p$ blocks. **UGA VIGRE conjecture.** The complexity of $S^\lambda$ is $w$ if and only if $\lambda$ is not $p\times p$. The complexity of a module is the least degree controlling the growth of the dimensions in a minimal projective resolution; the conjecture concerns when Specht modules attain the maximum complexity allowed by their block. It is motivated by the known maximal complexity of twisted Young modules and by limited results for simple modules, while the other direction remains open.
record.source_name: David J. Hemmer, “"Frobenius twists" in the representation theory of the symmetric group”, arXiv:1204.1045 (2012).
record.references:

record.title: Three-path conjecture for the maximum gap between average distance and proximity
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n\geq 3$ vertices. Let $\bar{l}$ denote its average distance and let $\pi$ denote its proximity, the minimum average distance from a vertex to all other vertices.

**Three-path conjecture.** Among all such graphs, the difference $\bar{l}-\pi$ is maximum for a graph composed of three paths of almost equal lengths with a common end point.

This conjecture concerns the extremal relationship between average distance and proximity in connected graphs. The source notes that several related conjectures had been posed, one of which had already been solved, but gives no resolution for this claim.
record.source_name: Jelena Sedlar, “Remoteness, proximity and few other distance invariants in graphs”, arXiv:1204.1184 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1184

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).

record.title: Cycle and crossed-edge extremal conjecture for remoteness minus radius
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n\geq 3$ vertices, with remoteness $\rho$, the maximum normalized transmission, and radius $r$.

**Remoteness–radius conjecture.** Then

$$
\rho-r\geq
\begin{cases}
\frac{3-n}{4},&\text{if }n\text{ is odd},\\
\frac{n^2}{4n-4}-\frac{n}{2},&\text{if }n\text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

The inequality is best possible: for even $n$ equality is attained by the cycle $C_n$, while for odd $n$ it is attained by the graph obtained from $C_n$ by adding two crossed edges on four successive vertices of the cycle.

This conjecture gives a sharp lower bound for the difference between remoteness and radius. The source does not state that the claim has been resolved.
record.source_name: Jelena Sedlar, “Remoteness, proximity and few other distance invariants in graphs”, arXiv:1204.1184 (2012).

record.title: Equality of the Chern-class slant-product homomorphisms
record.statement:
Let $\eta$ be the complex line bundle over $H^1(\Gamma;U(1))\times\check{\mathcal M}_{\Gamma}$ obtained from the equivariant ground-state line bundle, and let $\xi$ denote the comparison line bundle defined in the surrounding text. Slant product with their first Chern classes gives homomorphisms

$$
c_1(\eta)/,\ c_1(\xi)/:H_1(\check{\mathcal M}_{\Gamma};\mathbb Z)\to H_1(\Gamma;\mathbb Z).
$$

**Equality of the Chern-class slant-product homomorphisms.** The homomorphisms $c_1(\eta)/$ and $c_1(\xi)/$ coincide. This asserts that the analytically constructed line bundle and the comparison bundle determine the same homological invariant, but the supplied text gives no evidence that the assertion has been proved or refuted.
record.source_name: Vladimir Y. Chernyak, John R. Klein and Nikolai A. Sinitsyn, “Algebraic topology and the quantization of fluctuating currents”, arXiv:1204.2011 (2012).

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the normalized bosonic binding threshold
record.statement:
For each $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $Z_*(N)$ be the minimum nuclear charge needed to properly bind $N$ bosonic electrons, and define the normalized threshold

$$
\Lambda_*(N):=\frac{Z_*(N)}{N}.
$$

**Monotonicity conjecture.** The map $N\mapsto\Lambda_*(N)$ is monotonically increasing.

The source notes that $\Lambda_*(1)=0$, $0<\Lambda_*(2)\leq 1/2$, and that $\Lambda_*(N)$ tends to a limiting constant as $N$ tends to infinity. These facts do not imply the conjectured monotonicity, whose resolution is not given.
record.source_name: Michael K. -H. Kiessling, “The Hartree limit of Born's ensemble for the ground state of a bosonic atom or ion”, arXiv:1204.2511 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.2511

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2012). “I thank the referee for drawing my attention to this conjecture, which is mentioned as an open problem in Chpt.12 of .”

record.title: The discriminant dual-pair conjecture for umbral modules
record.statement: Let $H^{(\ell)}$ be an umbral vector-valued mock modular form, let $D$ be a discriminant of $H^{(\ell)}$, and let $K^{(\ell)}_{r,-D/4\ell}$ be the corresponding representation of $G^{(\ell)}$. Suppose that $D=-n\lambda^2$ for some integer $\lambda$, where $n$ is of the type considered in the source. A **dual pair** means a pair of dual irreducible representations, both of type $n$, occurring as irreducible constituents. **Discriminant dual-pair conjecture.** The representation $K^{(\ell)}_{r,-D/4\ell}$ contains at least one dual pair of irreducible representations of type $n$. The conjecture extends the preceding proposition from the smallest relevant discriminants to all discriminants of this form; it remains open in the source.

record.title: Finite-degree hyperbolicity-preserver conjecture for difference operators
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a constant-coefficient difference operator

$$
T(p(x))=a_0p(x)+a_1p(x-1)+\cdots+a_kp(x-k).
$$

It acts on hyperbolic polynomials of degree at most $m$ whose mesh is at least one, where the mesh is the minimum distance between consecutive roots. **Finite-degree difference analogue.** The operator $T$ preserves this set if and only if the polynomial $T((x)_m)$ is hyperbolic and has mesh at least one.

This is proposed as a finite-difference analogue of the finite-degree Hermite–Poulain theorem for constant-coefficient differential operators. Its status is open in the supplied source.

record.title: Strong level-set conjecture for independent sets in minimum-degree graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}(n,\delta)$ be the family of $n$-vertex graphs with minimum degree at least $\delta$, and let $i_t(G)$ denote the number of independent sets of size $t$ in $G$. **Strong level-set conjecture.** For each $\delta\geq 1$, $n\geq 2\delta$, $t\geq 3$, and $G\in\mathcal{G}(n,\delta)$,

$$
i_t(G)\leq i_t(K_{\delta,n-\delta}).
$$

This extends the weaker conjecture, which only asserts the inequality for sufficiently large $t$ depending on $\delta$. The source presents it as an evidence-based conjectural extension, and does not state that it has been proved.
record.source_name: John Engbers and David Galvin, “Counting independent sets of a fixed size in graphs with a given minimum degree”, arXiv:1204.3060 (2012).

record.title: Rational toral rank conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a nilpotent finite CW-complex. Its **rational torus rank** ${\operatorname{rk}}_0(X)$ is the largest integer $n$ for which a torus $T^n$ acts almost freely on a finite CW-complex having the same rational homotopy type as $X$. **Rational toral rank conjecture.** The total rational cohomology dimension satisfies

$$
\dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H^*(X,\mathbb{Q})\geq 2^{{\operatorname{rk}}_0(X)}.
$$

This is the rational formulation of the Halperin–Carlsson conjecture and connects torus actions with Sullivan models and rational homotopy theory. The source presents it as a longstanding conjecture.

record.title: Chartrand et al.'s realizability conjecture for metric and upper dimensions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. The **metric dimension** ${\rm dim}(G)$ is the minimum cardinality of a resolving set of $G$, and the **upper dimension** ${\rm dim}^+(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a minimal resolving set of $G$. For integers $a,b$ satisfying

$$
2\leq a\leq b,
$$

**Chartrand et al.'s realizability conjecture.** There exists a connected graph $G$ such that

$$
{\rm dim}(G)=a\quad\text{and}\quad {\rm dim}^+(G)=b.
$$

The conjecture asserts that every admissible pair of metric dimension and upper dimension is realizable; the source states that it was proved affirmatively in this paper.
record.source_name: Delia Garijo, Antonio González and Alberto Márquez, “On the metric dimension, the upper dimension and the resolving number of graphs”, arXiv:1205.1334 (2012).
record.references:

record.title: The local linear arboricity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let ${{\rm la}_{\ell}}(G)$ denote its local linear arboricity: the minimum number $j$ such that $G$ is covered by linear forests and every vertex belongs to at most $j$ of them.

**Local linear arboricity conjecture.** The value ${{\rm la}_{\ell}}(G)$ is either

$$
\left\lceil\frac{\Delta}{2}\right\rceil
$$

or

$$
\left\lceil\frac{\Delta+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This statement is necessary for the linear arboricity conjecture because local linear arboricity is at most ordinary linear arboricity. Its resolution status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Kolja Knauer and Torsten Ueckerdt, “Three ways to cover a graph”, arXiv:1205.1627 (2015).
record.references:

record.title: The local track-number conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let its local track-number be the minimum number of tracks in an injective track cover such that every vertex belongs to at most that many tracks.

**Local track-number conjecture.** The local track-number of $G$ is at most $3$.

The source identifies this as the only unresolved entry in its table of covering-number questions. It notes that the bound is known for bipartite planar graphs and for planar graphs of treewidth at most $3$, while the general planar case remains open.

record.title: Felsner–Krawczyk–Micek generalized crossing-vector conjecture
record.statement:
For $w\ge 1$ and integers $1\le k_1\le\cdots\le k_w$, say that two vectors $A,B\in\mathbb{Z}^w$ are $(k_1,\ldots,k_w)$-crossing if there are coordinates $i,j$ such that $A[i]-B[i]\ge k_i$ and $B[j]-A[j]\ge k_j$. Let $f(k_1,\ldots,k_w;w)$ be the maximum size of a subset of $\mathbb{Z}^w$ in which every two vectors are $1$-crossing but no two vectors are $(k_1,\ldots,k_w)$-crossing. **Felsner–Krawczyk–Micek generalized conjecture.** For $w\ge 1$ and $1\le k_1\le\cdots\le k_w$,

$$
f(k_1,\ldots,k_w;w)=k_2\cdots k_w.
$$

The paper notes that this apparently more general conjecture is equivalent to the main conjecture, since $f(k,w)=f(k,\ldots,k;w)$. The general case remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Groeneboom's cube-root-log local limit conjecture for interval-censoring case 2
record.statement:
Let $F_0$ and $H$ be continuously differentiable at $t_0$ and $(t_0,t_0)$, respectively, with strictly positive derivatives $f_0(t_0)$ and $h(t_0,t_0)$, where $H$ is the distribution function of $(T_i,U_i)$. Assume $0<F_0(t_0),H(t_0,t_0)<1$, and let $\hat F_n$ be the MLE of $F_0$. **Groeneboom's local limit conjecture.**

$$
(n\log n)^{1/3}\frac{\hat F_n(t_0)-F_0(t_0)}{\{\frac34 f_0(t_0)^2/h(t_0,t_0)\}^{1/3}}\stackrel{{\cal D}}\longrightarrow 2Z,
$$

where $Z$ is the last time that standard two-sided Brownian motion minus the parabola $y(t)=t^2$ reaches its maximum. This conjecture concerns the non-separated interval-censoring case, where observation intervals can be arbitrarily small.
record.source_name: Piet Groeneboom, “Nonparametric (smoothed) likelihood and integral equations”, arXiv:1205.1984 (2013).

record.title: The deviation conjectures for finite groups and subgroups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $H<G$. Define the **deviation** $\Delta(G,H)$ as the smallest natural number $\Delta$ such that $\Delta\cdot[H\backslash H]$ lies in the image of

$$
\operatorname{Res}\,\operatorname{Ind}:\mathcal{B}(H)\to\mathcal{B}(H).
$$

**Deviation conjectures.** With $\Delta=\Delta(G,H)$, one has $\Delta=1$ if and only if $H=G$, the index $[G:H]$ divides $\Delta$, and $\Delta$ divides $|G|$. These conjectures propose arithmetic constraints on the deviation, which measures both the failure of normality and the relative size of $H$ in $G$.

record.title: Log Approximation Rank Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $F$ be any two-party communication problem. Let $M_F$ be its communication matrix, let $\operatorname{rank}_{\epsilon'}(M_F)$ be the minimum rank of a matrix that $\epsilon'$-approximates $M_F$, and let $\mathbf{R}^{\epsilon}(F)$ denote the $\epsilon$-error randomized communication complexity. Here $\epsilon'$ is a constant depending on $\epsilon$. **Log Approximation Rank Conjecture.** There is a universal constant $c$ such that

$$
\log \operatorname{rank}_{\epsilon'}(M_F)\leq \mathbf{R}^{\epsilon}(F)\leq \log^c \operatorname{rank}_{\epsilon'}(M_F).
$$

The lower bound is known in the source's discussion; the conjecture asserts a matching polylogarithmic upper bound, which remains open.

record.title: Eigenvalue multiplicity scaling conjecture for cubic Julia sets
record.statement:
Let $\lambda_0=0$ be the lowest eigenvalue, and label consecutive eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots$ with multiplicity. For any eigenvalue $\lambda$, let $\#(\lambda)$ be the largest $n$ such that $\lambda_n=\lambda$.

**Eigenvalue multiplicity scaling conjecture.** For $p=3$,

$$
\#\left(3^{j\frac{k+1}{k}}\lambda\right)=3^j\#(\lambda).
$$

The claim concerns the location of derived eigenvalues in the spectrum and follows the observed scaling suggested by the multiplicatively periodic Weyl ratio. The source provides no resolution, so it remains open.

record.title: Independent-set extremal conjecture for graphs of prescribed minimum degree
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $\delta$, where $n$ and $\delta$ satisfy

$$
n \geq 2\delta.
$$

Let $i(G)$ denote the total number of independent sets in $G$, and let $K_{\delta,n-\delta}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $\delta$ and $n-\delta$.

**Minimum-degree extremal conjecture.** Under these hypotheses,

$$
i(G) \leq i(K_{\delta,n-\delta}).
$$

The paper proves the same conclusion under the stronger condition $n\geq (C-1)\delta^2+(3C-1)\delta+2$, where $C=\ln 4/(\ln 4-1)$, and conjectures that the relationship between $n$ and $\delta$ can be tightened considerably. The conjectured bound $n\geq 2\delta$ remains unresolved in the source.

record.title: Minh–Petitot polynomiality conjecture for the algebra of multiple zeta values
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{Z}$ denote the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra generated by all multiple zeta values. **Minh–Petitot conjecture.** The algebra $\mathcal{Z}$ is a polynomial algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$. This is a strong structural assertion that would imply algebraic independence of a suitable set of generators and determine the algebraic organization of multiple zeta values. The supplied source gives no evidence of a resolution, so its status is left open.
